title: Use exec for code, and keep ordinary environment separate from secret transport
summary: Current Colab CLI can execute a local Python file with colab exec -s NAME -f script.py; the CLI reads the file locally and sends its contents to the remote kernel, so a separate upload of the entrypoint is not inherently required. The qualified 0.6.0 build did not support exec --env. For that build, ordinary non-secret configuration was materialized inside the generated driver while secrets remained separately staged. This is a compatibility adaptation, not permission to embed secrets in source.
evidence_note: Current upstream documentation states that exec -f reads the local file and transmits it to the VM. Live 0.6.0 qualification rejected --env, so the adapter avoided the unsupported argv surface.
invariants: Never invent an --env surface without probing the installed CLI.
Ordinary configuration and secret material are different planes.
Driver generation is evidence-bearing source; anything embedded there may be logged or retained and must therefore be non-secret.
